quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get out of the way.
Stop right away and block the emergency vehicle.
Do everything you can to clear the path for the emergency vehicle.
Signal the emergency vehicle when it is safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do everything you can to clear the path for the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near, you must clear the path for it. If it is safe, pull to the side of the road to let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.question: A U-turn is not allowed:

options.text: In a parking lot.
On or near curves or hills.
On a straight road where you can see 500 feet ahead in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near curves or hills.
questions.explanation: Never turn around on or near a curve or hill. You may not see oncoming traffic or people and could cause a crash.

questions.question: You can legally pass on the right side of another vehicle when:

options.text: The vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an open passing lane.
You drive off the road to pass.
You are on a narrow bridge.
You can pass anytime.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an open passing lane.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right of a vehicle turning left if there is an open passing lane. You may also pass on the right on a road with two or more lanes going the same way. Never drive off the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, it:

options.text: Slows your reaction time.
Makes you feel less sure of yourself.
Breaks down in your body faster.
Reduces driving mistakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows your reaction time.
questions.explanation: As alcohol builds up in your body, it slows your reaction time, makes you feel more confident, and causes you to make more driving mistakes.

questions.question: You are angry after something happened at work. When you get to your car, you should:

options.text: Play loud music so you do not think about it.
Drive fast on the highway to release your anger.
Wait a few minutes to calm down before you start driving.
Stop at a bar and drink before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait a few minutes to calm down before you start driving.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, wait to calm down before driving. Driving while emotional is dangerous and puts you and others at risk.

questions.question: A painted arrow on the road means:

options.text: Drivers in that lane may make the turn shown by the arrow if they want to.
Drivers in that lane must make the turn shown by the arrow only if traffic lights are broken.
Drivers in that lane must always stop before making the turn shown by the arrow.
Drivers in that lane must make the turn shown by the arrow while following traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers in that lane must make the turn shown by the arrow while following traffic signals.
questions.explanation: A painted arrow in a lane tells drivers they must make the turn shown. Always follow traffic signs or signals before turning in the direction of the arrow.

questions.question: It is safe to stop on railroad tracks for a short time if you are moving with traffic.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Never stop, stand, or park on railroad tracks. Always make sure your entire vehicle can cross the tracks before you drive onto them.

questions.question: On a two-way road, when an emergency vehicle approaches with a siren and flashing lights, you should:

options.text: Drive slowly until it passes.
Speed up to clear the road.
Pull to the right side and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side and stop.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass. Pull to the right edge of the road when you see or hear a police car, fire truck, ambulance, or other emergency vehicle with a siren or lights coming from any direction.

questions.question: You must follow the directions of school crossing guards:

options.text: At all times.
Only during school hours.
Only if you see children present.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Always watch for crossing guards near schools and always follow their directions.

questions.question: The best safety restraints in a crash are:

options.text: A lap and shoulder belt only.
An airbag only.
Both a lap and shoulder belt and an airbag.
No safety restraints.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap and shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts greatly improve your chances of surviving a crash and avoiding serious injury. Airbags work best when used with safety belts. Always wear both a shoulder belt and a lap belt.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.

options.text: Increase
Maintain
Vary
Reduce

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce
questions.explanation: Slow down when turning. This helps you stay in your lane, control your vehicle, and react to unexpected situations.

questions.question: Taking drugs along with alcohol:

options.text: Increases the risk of causing a crash.
Is no more dangerous than consuming alcohol by itself.
Lessens the effect of alcohol on your ability to drive.
Has no effect on your general driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of causing a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs (illegal, prescription, and over-the-counter) can impair your thinking and driving ability. Mixing alcohol with drugs makes this danger even worse and increases your crash risk.

questions.question: At night, it is hardest to see:

options.text: Road signs.
Pedestrians.
Other motorists.
Street lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than signs or other objects on the roadway.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: Pass the vehicle as slowly as possible.
Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.
Pass the vehicle as safely and as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass the vehicle as safely and as quickly as possible.
questions.explanation: Pass quickly and safely to keep the passing zone brief. Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: Sudden wind gusts on highways:

options.text: Generally affect only the movement of large vehicles.
Only cause visibility problems.
Can cause problems for all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause problems for all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind can affect any vehicle, not just large ones. Wind can reduce visibility by blowing dust and dirt onto the road. It can also physically push vehicles across lanes.

questions.question: The driver's left arm and hand are extended downward. This hand signal means that the driver plans to:

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Start up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: When a driver extends their left arm downward, they are signaling that they plan to stop. Adjust your driving if you see this signal from a driver ahead of you.

questions.question: If worried, nervous, angry, or crying, a driver:

options.text: Will drive no differently than they would if they were thinking more clearly.
Can drive faster because they are more in touch with their senses.
Should take the time to focus on driving before starting the engine.
Should call a friend to vent while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should take the time to focus on driving before starting the engine.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions can distract you from driving safely. Your mind focuses on your feelings instead of the road. Calm down and focus before you start driving.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: No right turn.
Drive only in the direction of the arrow.
Curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive only in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers to travel only in the direction shown by the arrow. You must follow this traffic law.

questions.question: If you find yourself in a skid:

options.text: Brake lightly.
Stay off the brakes.
Brake abruptly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: Do not use your brakes during a skid. Braking will make the skid worse.

questions.question: When entering a street from a driveway, you:

options.text: Must drive slowly to allow approaching vehicles and pedestrians time to get out of your way.
Must honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to give you room.
Must stop and proceed only when there are no pedestrians or vehicles approaching.
Can disregard any pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop and proceed only when there are no pedestrians or vehicles approaching.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the street from a driveway. Yield to pedestrians and vehicles. Stop before crossing the sidewalk. It is against the law to fail to stop.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions can hurt your driving ability. Worry, excitement, fear, anger, or sadness can make it hard to drive safely. Stress reduces your concentration. It is better to wait to drive than to drive when you are emotionally upset.

questions.question: A flashing red light on a traffic signal means:

options.text: The same thing as a stop sign.
The traffic signal is broken.
You do not have to come to a complete stop.
Driving conditions are dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: You notice a vehicle defect that may affect safe operation. You should:

options.text: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
Fix the defect when you can afford it.
Drive slower.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Fix any defect that may affect safe driving as soon as possible. Fix defects before you drive the vehicle.

questions.question: A driver turning left at an intersection must yield to a bicyclist coming from the opposite direction.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming bicycles just as you would to oncoming cars. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn. Go only when it is safe and no traffic or pedestrians are coming.

questions.question: If you see a stopped school bus with flashing lights and a signal arm extended, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Go 15 mph if no children are outside.
Go at normal speed and watch for children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: You must stop completely when you see a school bus with flashing lights and arm extended. Stay stopped until the arm goes back and the bus moves. This applies whether you are going the same direction or opposite direction.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road curves left then right.
The road curves right then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right then left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the road curves right first, then curves left. Slow down to safely stay on the road.

questions.question: When can you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never go around or under a lowered gate at a railroad crossing. After the gate is raised, only cross the tracks when you can see clearly in both directions and are certain no trains are coming.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Curves ahead.
Divided highway starts.
Divided highway ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the divided highway is ending ahead. Be ready to change lanes or move your position.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle, a driver of a small vehicle must be prepared for:

options.text: Loud noises.
Excess air pollution.
Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
Falling vehicle parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles sideways. Drivers of small vehicles should be ready to steer carefully when passing or approaching large vehicles moving at high speeds.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?

options.text: Whoever started moving last.
The driver.
Whoever is slower.
The pedestrian.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver.
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, with or without a crosswalk.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Stop before entering the intersection.
Slow down and proceed carefully.
Wait for a green light before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and look for cross traffic. Then proceed carefully.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light means the same thing as a:

options.text: Solid red light.
Stop sign.
Yield sign.
Caution sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop completely, just like a stop sign. Come to a full stop and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: How can you check your blind spot before changing lanes?

options.text: Look in your inside rearview mirror.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Look in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show blind spots. You must turn your head and look over your shoulder to see areas that mirrors cannot show.

questions.question: What does a steady yellow light at an intersection mean?

options.text: Go.
Yield to other cars.
Slow down and get ready to stop.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming soon. Slow down and prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through with care.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: One outside mirror removes all blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than regular cars.
You can see blind spots by looking in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than regular cars.
questions.explanation: All vehicles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than regular passenger cars.
